mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES at t-0w signals immediate suppression of commuting and discretionary foot traffic, which will pull RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks as fewer trips are made to stores and restaurants.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below its last-4-week mean for the next 28 days despite continued negative TRANSIT and WORKPLACES readings.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates people are staying home more, substituting away from shopping trips and reducing RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above +5 and stays there for at least 2 weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days after RESIDENTIAL remains above +5 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM rises while PARKS remains flat or negative, people are likely substituting essential trips for discretionary outings, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior 4-week mean when GROCERY_PHARM is positive and PARKS stays at or below zero.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls by more than 15 points week-on-week, it marks a restriction or avoidance shock that propagates into retail visits with a one-week lag, pushing RETAIL_REC lower.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline in the week after TRANSIT drops by more than 15 points.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL indicates stockpiling and home-confinement behavior, which should suppress discretionary retail demand over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days while both GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL remain elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A positive PARKS reading combined with higher RETAIL_REC in the same week reflects fair-weather discretionary activity, which should keep retail and recreation above its recent average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its last-4-week mean for the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining positive or improving.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in WORKPLACES from negative to positive territory signals normalization of daytime activity, and that restored routine should lift RETAIL_REC with a two-week lag.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses from negative to positive week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w WORKPLACES = -13.1 after positive readings in t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days after WORKPLACES moves from below zero to above zero.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both weaken at the same time, the city is entering a broader mobility suppression regime that reduces incidental shopping trips and drives RETAIL_REC down over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w shows sharp declines in both series
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its prior 4-week average over the next 28 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are declining.
